Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
914 PM EDT Tue Sep 8 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Nudged down low temperatures slightly in outlying areas given
mostly clear skies and light winds tonight.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Mostly dry through Wednesday.

- 2) Shower and thunderstorm chances return Thursday.

- 3) Cooler and less humid conditions are expected on Friday,
  before humidity builds back in this weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Mostly dry through Wednesday.

Conditions will remain tranquil as high pressure persists over 
the Mid-Atlantic through Wednesday before gradually moving 
offshore. Large scale subsidence and dry air lead to a mostly
precipitation-free forecast with temperatures rising to several 
degrees above normal as the high pulls offshore.

A weak surface trough in the wake of gradually departing high
pressure may be enough to produce a few showers mainly over the
Shenandoah Valley/I-81 corridor into the eastern WV panhandle
from late Wednesday morning through late Wednesday afternoon.

High temperatures may approach 90 Wednesday (slightly cooler in
the mountains). Low temperatures (and dew points) will be in 
the 50s and 60s during this time. Some river valley fog is 
likely each morning.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Shower and thunderstorm chances return Thursday.

The upper-level ridge will begin to flatten out Wednesday before 
breaking down and pushing south and east into Thursday. Several 
pieces of upper-level energy rotating around an upper low 
centered over Hudson Bay will slowly push a cold front south 
towards our region by Thursday. At the surface, high pressure 
pushing offshore will bring increasing warmth and moisture 
to the area, with highs in the 80s to near 90 especially south
of US-50/I-66 with dew points in the upper 60s to low 70s. Mid-
level moisture will be increasing on westerly flow, but that
introduces a downsloping component in the lower levels. This
reduces the amount of CAPE/DCAPE, especially when given
anticipated cloud cover over the northern half of the area, for
any potential severe weather. Still, a few clusters particularly
from central VA to southern MD could contain gusty winds and
heavy downpours Thursday, mainly in the afternoon and evening.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Cooler and less humid conditions are expected 
on Friday, before humidity builds back in this weekend. 

High pressure will build to our north on Friday in the wake of 
Thursday's frontal passage. Cooler and drier air will advect into 
the region from the north in advance of the approaching high.
Partly to mostly sunny skies are expected, with high temperatures
in the upper 70s and lower 80s. It will also feel considerably 
less humid, with dewpoints dropping into the upper 50s and lower
60s. Some shower or thunderstorm activity is possible near and
south of I-64 as the front stalls just off to the south.

High pressure will move offshore and a strong area of low pressure 
will track across Hudson Bay on Saturday, causing winds to turn out 
of the south in response. Southerly winds will advect a more humid 
airmass back into the area, with dewpoints climbing into the upper 
60s and lower 70s. Chances for showers and thunderstorms will 
accompany the more humid airmass. Both instability and shear values 
are forecast to remain relatively modest, so any storms that do
form likely stay on the weaker side.

There is still some model divergence for Sunday. What we do know is 
that the humidity will stick around, bringing chances for showers 
and thunderstorms. However, there is still some uncertainty as to 
whether or not the marine layer will mix out. If not, temperatures 
will be cooler with plenty of clouds. If so, there will be some 
breaks of sunshine and it will be warmer. Guidance leans slightly 
toward the second scenario, but this will have to be monitored as it 
gets closer.

High pressure may return behind a weak cold front for Monday and 
Tuesday, bringing drier conditions, but temperatures will most 
likely still be above climo.

&&

.AVIATION /01Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
VFR conditions are expected to prevail through the end of the
week, with two exceptions. Early morning river valley fog could
affect mainly KCHO/KMRB each day roughly 08z-13z (confidence too
low to include in TAF as of 00Z). Then, some shower and t-storm
activity could bring brief restrictions on Thursday (mainly in 
the afternoon and/or evening). Winds remain S/SW through 
Wednesday night (with some gusts up to 20 kt possible Wednesday 
afternoon) until a cold front brings a shift to W/NW Thursday
morning.

Low clouds are possible late Friday night into Saturday with
sub-VFR conditions. Showers are possible Saturday along with a 
possible afternoon thunderstorm.

&&

.MARINE...
Winds may increase in modest channeling tonight over the lower
tidal Potomac River and the main channel of the Chesapeake Bay.
Through 9 PM, winds have held below advisory thresholds, but
it's possible they tick up a bit from midnight through 10 AM or
so. Will monitor for potential of a short fused advisory. Winds 
are more likely to increase Wednesday afternoon into Wednesday 
night, when advisories will be in effect for all waters. Winds 
shift to the west and northwest and could remain gusty Thursday 
as a cold front crosses, possibly bringing a few showers and 
thunderstorms.

Sub-SCA level north to northwesterly winds are most likely over the 
waters on Friday. Winds will shift to the south on Saturday, and 
could near low-end SCA levels within channeled southerly flow 
Saturday afternoon into Saturday evening.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tide levels are now dropping lower than one foot above normal,
and light flow may allow anomalies to persist at these levels
through Wednesday. Unless there is a sudden rebound, it appears
less likely Annapolis will reach minor flood stage during this
time. Other sites could approach minor flood at times, as well,
mainly late Wednesday night into early Thursday morning, though
west-of-south flow by this time lowers confidence. More notable
water level decreases will occur Thursday behind a cold front.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...None.
MD...Small Craft Advisory from 1 PM Wednesday to 7 AM EDT Thursday 
     for MDZ008.
VA...None.
WV...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory from 1 PM Wednesday to 7 AM EDT Thursday 
     for ANZ530>533-538>542.
     Small Craft Advisory from 4 PM Wednesday to 10 AM EDT Thursday 
     for ANZ534-537-543.
     Small Craft Advisory from 4 PM Wednesday to 4 AM EDT Thursday 
     for ANZ535-536.

&&

$$
